To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) C4A binds to the 38‐kDa serum protein, but C4B does not, (2) C4A and 38‐kDA are present in a 1:1 stoichiometric complex in serum, (3) C4A is more active in the classical pathway than C4B, (4) C4A covalently binds to the immune complex, but C4A also binds non‐covalently, (5)
C4A, more than C4B, binds to the BSA‐anti‐BSA immune complex when the C4 proteins are isolated, but in serum C4A and 4B bind to similar extents to this complex.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the binding of C3 and C4 to an immune complex as it occurs in human serum and the effect of serum concentration on the amount of binding.
the binding of C2 to C4B and C4A in the presence of an immune complex and the binding of these proteins to serum proteins.
the binding of C3 and C4 to an immune complex.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
C4A and B bind equally to the BSA immune complex in serum, but that there are differences in the binding of C2 and C4 to the complex in the presence and absence of other serum proteins.
the in vivo binding to immune complexes is different from that of isolated proteins, and that this difference is due to the presence of serum proteins.
in serum C4A and B bind to an immune complex with a 1 : 1 ratio, but the mechanism of binding is complex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
C4A and B bind to an immune complex with equal affinity and in serum the amount of C4A bound to a complex is not higher than that of C4B.
the binding of C3 to immune complexes in serum is not a passive process but is dependent on the presence of other serum proteins.
C4A and B bind in a similar manner to the immune complex and that the differences in binding between isoforms are due to the presence of serum proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
when studying the binding of C3 or C4 to immune complexes, it is important to use the proteins in the context of serum.
the binding of C3 and C4 to an immune complex is not a simple process and that the use of isolated proteins may not reflect what occurs in serum.
the binding of the C 4 isoforms to a complex may be affected by serum proteins.
